title: Khufu
objective: After this level you can describe what we know about the builder of the Great Pyramid.
summary: Khufu built the Great Pyramid, yet few written sources about him remain. His only named statue is a 7.5 cm ivory figure, and Herodotus gave him a bad reputation that Egyptians did not share.

cards.headline: The Great Pyramid’s builder survives as a statue you could hide in your hand.
cards.body: The only known statue of Khufu with his name on it is an ivory figure 7.5 cm tall. Khufu built the Great Pyramid at Giza. The man himself is nearly a stranger.

cards.headline: The man behind the pyramid
cards.body: Khufu, called Cheops by the Greeks, was the second king of the 4th Dynasty and the son of King Sneferu. He ruled in the Old Kingdom, the age of the great pyramids, and built the Great Pyramid at Giza. Yet few written sources about his life remain. We know his tomb far better than we know him.

cards.headline: Lost and found in the dirt
cards.body: The ivory statuette was found by Flinders Petrie at Abydos in 1903. It shows Khufu on a throne wearing the red crown of Lower Egypt (remember Level 6?). During the dig its head was knocked off and lost; three weeks later the team found it by sifting the excavated dirt. The builder of the Great Pyramid, rescued from a spoil heap by a sieve.

mascot.line: Three weeks of sifting dirt for one tiny ivory head. Archaeology rewards patience.

cards.headline: A bad review, two thousand years late
cards.body: Herodotus, the Greek historian from Level 2, wrote some 2,000 years after Khufu. He called the reigns of Khufu and his son Khafre 106 years of oppression and misery. Yet in Egypt itself, Khufu was remembered after his death as a wise ruler. Whose review would you trust: a visitor two thousand years late, or the people who kept his memory?

cards.headline: Khufu: met
learned: Khufu (Cheops) built the Great Pyramid in the Old Kingdom
Few written sources about his life remain
His only named statue is a 7.5 cm ivory figure
Herodotus called his reign oppressive; Egyptians remembered him as wise

questions.prompt: How tall is the ivory statuette of Khufu found at Abydos?

options.label: 75 cm
options.rationale: It is ten times smaller than that.

options.label: 20 metres
options.rationale: That is the size of Ramesses’ statues at Abu Simbel.

questions.explanation: The only known statue of Khufu bearing his name is just 7.5 cm tall.

questions.prompt: Why do historians know so little about Khufu as a person?

options.label: His name was never written down
options.rationale: His name is on his statuette.

options.label: He ruled for only a few weeks
options.rationale: He ruled long enough to build the Great Pyramid.

options.label: The Greeks destroyed his records
options.rationale: The simple problem is that few sources survive.

options.label: Few written sources about his life remain

questions.explanation: Although he built the Great Pyramid, few written sources about Khufu’s life survive.

questions.prompt: Khufu built the Great Pyramid at Giza. From Level 1, which age of Egypt was he part of?

options.label: The Middle Kingdom
options.rationale: That came centuries after the great pyramids.

options.label: The New Kingdom
options.rationale: That was the age of Tutankhamun and Ramesses.

questions.explanation: Khufu was a 4th Dynasty king of the Old Kingdom, the age of the great pyramids.
